title: Heraclides confesses; the Son was God before the body
english: When the bishops present had opened a discussion of bishop Heraclides' faith, so that he might confess before them all how he believes, and each had said what came to him and had asked his questions, bishop Heraclides spoke.

Heraclides said: I too believe what the divine scriptures say: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. This was in the beginning with God. All things came to be through him, and without him not even one thing came to be. Do we then agree in the faith? And according to this, do we also believe that Christ has taken flesh, that he was born, that he went up into the heavens in the flesh in which he rose, that he sits at the right hand of the Father, about to come from there and judge the living and the dead — God and man?

Origen said: Since an examination is taking place once for all, I will speak to the point under examination. The whole church is present and listening. One church ought not to differ in knowledge from another church. If you lie, you are not a church. I ask you, Bishop Heraclides: God is the Almighty, the unbegotten, the one who has made the universe over all things. Are you content with this?
Heraclides said: I am content. I too believe this.
Origen said: Christ Jesus was in the form of God, and he is other than the God in whose form he was. Was he God before he came into a body, or not?
Heraclides said: He was God before.
Origen said: Was he God before he came into a body, or not?
Heraclides said: Yes.
Origen said: Another God besides this God in whose form he himself was?

added_allusions.reason: Heraclides quotes the prologue as his confession.
Judge the living and the dead.
Same living-and-dead judgment formula.
Quoted: being in the form of God.
Sits at the right hand of the Father (with Ps 110:1).
Right-hand session behind the confession.

translator_notes: Title from DCO [00001], before Scherer [1].
πάπα Ἡρακλείδα rendered 'Bishop Heraclides'. Greek πάπα is the address to a sitting bishop, not later 'Pope'; 'papa' in English sounds odd and misleads.
ἀγένητος rendered 'unbegotten' (one nu in the dump).
Origen repeats the pre-body question; the doubling is kept.
DCO prints Ὠριγένῃς once; treated as Ὠριγένης.

title: Two Gods, and one power
english: Heraclides said: Clearly he is of another, and being in that one's form he belongs to the one who created all things.

Origen said: So then the only-begotten Son of God, the firstborn of all creation, was God, the Son of God — and we need not be over-scrupulous in saying, in one respect, two Gods, and in another respect, one God?

Heraclides said: What you say is clear. But we say that God is the Almighty, God without beginning, without end, containing all things and not contained; and that his Word is the Son of the living God, God and man, through whom all things have come to be — God according to spirit, man according to his birth from Mary.
Origen said: What I asked, you do not seem to have answered. Make it clear, then; perhaps I did not follow. Is the Father God?
Heraclides said: Entirely.
Origen said: Is the Son other than the Father?
Heraclides said: How can he be a son, if he is also father?
Origen said: The Son, being other than the Father — is he also God?
Heraclides said: He too is God.
Origen said: And do the two become one?
Heraclides said: Yes.
Origen said: Do we confess two Gods?
Heraclides said: Yes; the power is one.

Origen said: But our brothers take offense at there being two Gods. So the wording must be tended with care, and we must show in what respect they are two, and in what respect the two are one God. The divine scriptures have taught that many twos are one — and not only two. Even some things more than two, and even things far more in number, they have taught to be one. The task before us now is not to take a problem and skip past it and string words together, but to chew it, for the simpler people, as if it were meat, and to put the word into the hearers' ears little by little.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: firstborn of all creation.
Only-begotten of God.
Through whom all things have come to be.
In the form of the Creator.

translator_notes: ἴσως kept as 'perhaps I did not follow'.
δεισιδαιμονοῦμεν: 'we need not be over-scrupulous' (religious scruple at saying two Gods), not later 'demon-fear' jargon.
θεραπευτέον τὸν λόγον: 'the wording must be tended with care' (healed/cared for), not 'therapy'.
Scherer [3] splits πρόβλημα; hanging clause completed here so the section can be read alone.

title: How two are one: flesh, spirit, God
english: Origen went on: The task is not to take a problem and skip past it and string words together, but to chew it, for the simpler people, as if it were meat, and to put the word into the hearers' ears little by little.

Many twos, then, are said in the scriptures to be one. Which scriptures? Adam is one person; the woman is another. Adam is other than the woman, and the woman other than the man. And it is said at once in the Making of the World that the two are one: For the two shall be into one flesh. So then it is possible at times for two to be one flesh.
But keep this for me: in the case of Adam and Eve it is not said that the two shall be into one spirit, nor that the two shall be into one soul, but the two shall be into one flesh.

The righteous man again, being other than Christ, is said by the apostle to be one toward Christ: For he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit. Is it not that the one is of a lesser, lower, inferior substance, and Christ of a more divine, more glorious, more blessed? Therefore they are no longer two?

For the man and the woman are no longer two but one flesh, and the righteous human being and Christ are one spirit. So our Savior and Lord, toward the Father and God of all, is not one flesh, nor one spirit, but what is above both flesh and spirit: one God.

For it was necessary that, in the case of human beings joined to one another, the name 'flesh' should be set; and in the case of a righteous human being joined to Christ, the name 'spirit'; and in the case of Christ being united to the Father, neither the name 'flesh' nor the name 'spirit' should be set, but what is more honorable than these: the name 'God.'

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: the two shall be into one flesh.
Gospel form of the same two-one-flesh saying.
Quoted: joined to the Lord, one spirit.
Quoted: no longer two but one flesh.

translator_notes: διαμασήσασθαι kept as 'chew' with Origen's meat image; not smoothed to 'digest'.
Κοσμοποιΐα rendered 'Making of the World' (Genesis 1–2), not 'Hexaemeron'.
Page-cut from §2 completed with a lead-in; last sentence completed from §4 so the section stands alone.

title: I and the Father are one; offering to God through God
english: Origen went on: In the case of Christ united to the Father, neither the name 'flesh' nor the name 'spirit' should be set, but what is more honorable than these: the name 'God.' Hence let us understand I and the Father are one in this way.

Let us pray — on account of those who keep the dyad, and on account of those who introduce the monad — so that we neither fall into the opinion of those who have split from the church into a fantasy of monarchy, doing away with the Son from the Father and in power doing away with the Father as well, nor fall into another impious teaching, the one that denies the divinity of Christ.

How then do the divine scriptures speak, as in Before me no other God came to be, and after me there shall not be, and in I am, and there is no God besides me? With these utterances we must not suppose that the 'one' as applied to the God of all [lacuna] is apart from Christ; nor indeed Christ apart from God. But let us say that they are in the way Jesus says, I and my Father are one.

We have to work at these words, because many things have been stirred in this church. They often write that people should subscribe, and that the bishop should subscribe, and those under suspicion, and subscribe before the whole people, so that there may no longer be faction or any inquiry about this.

With God permitting, then, and secondly the bishops, and thirdly the presbyters and the people too, I will speak again of what is stirring me at this point. The offering is always made to God Almighty through Jesus Christ, as offering his divinity to the Father. Let the offering not be made twice, but to God through God.
I shall seem bold in speaking, as we pray to remain in the covenants. If it does not happen, you shall not take a man's face nor marvel at a ruler's face.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted twice: I and the Father are one (second time with 'my Father').
Quoted: before me no other God came to be.
Quoted: I am, and there is no God besides me (with Deut 32:39).
Same 'no God besides me' form.
Quoted: you shall not take a man's face (partial; continues on next page).
Face of a ruler; with Lev 19:15.

translator_notes: Εὐχώμεθα kept as 'Let us pray' (locked letters). τοὺς τηροῦντες / τοὺς ἐμποιοῦντες are nominative after τοὺς; likely τηροῦντας / ἐμποιοῦντας, not silently emended.
φαντασίαν μοναρχίας: 'fantasy of monarchy' (the monarchian split), not later 'Monarchianism' as a school label in the reading text.
† τῷ ἀχράντῳ left untranslated as [lacuna]; no conjecture filled.
προσφορὰ: 'offering' (doxology/eucharist), twice-not-once: to God through God.
Leviticus 19:15 quote completed at the section end so it does not hang; the next page opens the covenants stretch.

title: Covenants; a dead body, not a spiritual one
english: [lacuna — several words around 'bishop' and 'covenants' are daggered and unreadable]. If this is not done, [lacuna] these covenants would give occasions for inquiries [lacuna]. A bishop or a presbyter is not a bishop, is not a presbyter; if a deacon, he is not a deacon nor a layman; if he is a layman, he is not a layman, nor is he gathered in the assembly. If it seems good, let these covenants be made.

Some add that, as to the matters of the divinity, offering the divinity in this way, in substance, to Jesus Christ, I have confessed the resurrection of a dead body before the church. And since our Savior and Lord took a body, let us examine what the body was.

The church alone, against all the heresies that deny the resurrection, confesses the resurrection of a dead body, as following from the firstfruits having been raised from the dead, that the dead are raised. Christ the firstfruits: for this reason his body became a dead body. For if his body had not become dead — able to be wrapped in linen, to receive myrrh and whatever else belongs to the dead, and to be laid in a tomb — a spiritual body cannot suffer these things. For it is in no way possible for what is spiritual to be made dead, or for what is spiritual to become without sensation. If a spiritual thing can be made dead, there is a fear that after the resurrection of the dead, when our body is raised according to the apostle who says, It is sown a soulish body, it is raised a spiritual body, we may all die.

added_allusions.reason: End of the face/ruler quotation from the previous page.
Christ the firstfruits.
Firstfruits, then those who are Christ's.
Linen and myrrh for the dead body.
Wrapped and laid in a tomb.
Quoted: sown soulish, raised spiritual (sentence continues in section 6).

translator_notes: Opening of Scherer [5] is the worst stretch in the locked dump (αν †, ουτ †, και ναι †). Rendered as [lacuna], not reconstructed.
ψυχικόν kept as 'soulish' so the ψυχή in the word is visible; 'natural' would hide it.
Confidence for this page: uncertain on the covenant-penalty clause; source_verified on the resurrection argument.
1 Corinthians 15:44 completed across the Scherer cut so the section does not hang.

title: Christ dies no more; Maximus; spirit, soul, body
english: Origen went on from the apostle's word — It is sown a soulish body, it is raised a spiritual body — lest, if a spiritual thing can be made dead, we may all die. For Christ, raised from the dead, dies no more. And not only does Christ, raised from the dead, die no more, but also those who are Christ's, once raised from the dead, die no more. If these things please, these too, on the testimony of the people, shall be enacted and fixed. What else concerning the faith? Do these things seem good to you, Maximus, [lacuna]?

Maximus said: May it come about that all become like me. Before God and the church I both subscribe and anathematize. Only, lest I be wholly in doubt and double-minded, I ask about a certain point [corrupt stretch]. For the brothers know that I used to say: I have to be benefited by the brother and taught this. If the spirit has been handed over to the Father according to Father, into your hands I commit my spirit, and the spirit is apart, the flesh having died and lying in a tomb — when it is opened, how do the dead rise?

Origen said: We have learned from the holy scriptures that the human being is composite. For the apostle says: May God sanctify your spirit and the soul and the body; and May he sanctify you wholly, and may your spirit and the soul and the body be kept complete, blamelessly, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. This spirit is not the Holy Spirit, but a part of the human being's constitution, as the same apostle teaches when he says: The Spirit bears witness with our spirit. For if it were the Holy Spirit, he would not have said: The Spirit bears witness with our spirit.

added_allusions.reason: End of the soulish/spiritual quotation.
Quoted: Christ raised dies no more.
Those who are Christ's.
Quoted: into your hands I commit my spirit.
Source of the Lucan commit-spirit saying (LXX 30:6).
Quoted, in two slightly disordered forms in the dump: spirit, soul, body kept whole.
Quoted: the Spirit bears witness with our spirit.

translator_notes: † ειπεναι at the Maximus address not filled; likely εἰπεῖν / εἰρηκέναι.
† in Maximus's 'lest I be double-minded' clause marked, not rewritten.
1 Thess 5:23 appears twice, slightly out of order; both forms translated as printed.
Human πνεῦμα distinguished from Holy Spirit, as Origen insists.
Romans 8:16 completed at the section end so it does not hang mid-quote.

title: The whole man taken up; deposit of the spirit
english: Origen went on: The Spirit bears witness with our spirit. If it were the Holy Spirit, he would not have said it that way.

Our Savior and Lord, then, wanting to save a human being in the way he wanted to save, for this reason wanted to save a body in this way, as he likewise wanted to save a soul, and he wanted to save the remaining part of the human being as well, the spirit. The whole human being would not have been saved if he had not taken up the whole human being.

They set aside the salvation of the human body when they say the Savior's body is spiritual. They set aside the salvation of the human spirit, about which the apostle says: No one among men knows the things of the man except the spirit of the man that is in him. Wanting to save the spirit of the man, about which the apostle said these things, he took up a human spirit as well.

These three were divided at the time of the Passion; these three were united at the time of the resurrection. At the time of the Passion they were divided. How? The body in the tomb, the soul in Hades, the spirit he committed to the Father. The soul in Hades: You will not abandon my soul to Hades. If he committed the spirit to the Father, he has given the spirit as a deposit. It is one thing to grant as a gift, another to hand over, another to place as a deposit. The one who places a deposit places it in order to receive the deposit back. To whom, then, did the spirit have to commit the deposit, if not to the Father?

This is above me and my condition and my mind; for I am not of such stature as to say that just as the body could not go down into Hades — even if those who call Jesus' body spiritual say this — so neither could the spirit go down into Hades, and therefore he gave the spirit as a deposit to the Father until he should rise from the dead.

added_allusions.reason: End of the witness quotation.
Quoted: no one knows the things of the man except the man's spirit.
Quoted: you will not abandon my soul to Hades (LXX 15:10; Acts 2:27).
Peter's use of the same psalm of the resurrection.
Spirit committed to the Father.

translator_notes: παρακαταθήκη kept as 'deposit' (something placed to be received back), distinct from gift and from handing-over.
Origen's hedge ὑπὲρ ἐμέ / οὐ γάρ εἰμι τηλικοῦτος kept; he then states the Hades argument anyway.
Σωτῆ ρος joined as Σωτῆρος.
Hades clause completed from the next Scherer page so the hedge does not hang.

title: Do not touch me; faith and life together
english: Origen went on: I am not of such stature as to say that just as the body could not go down into Hades — even if those who call Jesus' body spiritual say this — so neither could the spirit go down into Hades, and therefore he gave the spirit as a deposit to the Father until he should rise from the dead.

Having committed this deposit to the Father, he receives it back. When? Not at the same moment as the resurrection, but immediately after the resurrection. Bring me the gospel writing as witness. The Lord Jesus Christ rose from the dead. Mary met him, and he says to her: Do not touch me. For he wanted the one who touched him to touch him as complete, so that by touching him complete she might be benefited — the body from the body, the soul from the soul, the spirit from the spirit. For I have not yet gone up to the Father. He goes up to the Father and comes to the disciples. So then he goes up to the Father. For what? To receive the deposit back.

The matters of the faith, as many as have been indicated to us, have been examined together. But we should know that we are judged in the divine court not concerning faith only, as if life were not examined, nor concerning life only, as if faith were not searched. When both are set right we are justified; when both are not set right we are punished for both. There are some who will not be punished for both but for the one: some for the faith as having stumbled, but not for the life as not having been set right; and others, conversely, will not be punished for the faith, but will be punished for the life, as having lived contrary to the right word.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: Do not touch me; I have not yet gone up to the Father.
He comes to the disciples after the ascent implied here.

translator_notes: οὐχ ἅμα τῇ ἀναστάσει, ἀλλ' εὐθέως μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν kept as two moments: not at the rising itself, but immediately after.
ἔσηνεν uncertain in the dump (perhaps ἔσηνεν from σημαίνω 'indicated', or ἔσεισεν 'shook'). Rendered 'have been indicated'; not silently replaced.
Mary's touch: Origen's three-part benefit (body/soul/spirit) kept layered.
Faith-and-life contrast completed across the page cut.

title: Pure heart and clean hands; lesser sins too
english: Origen went on: Some will not be punished for both, but for the one. Some for the faith, as having stumbled, but not for the life, as not having been set right; and others, conversely, will not be punished for the faith, but will be punished for the life, as having lived contrary to the right word.

I think that in Solomon's Proverbs these two generic things — I mean the matter of how we believe and know, and the matter of how we live — are spoken by Solomon in this way: Who will boast of having a pure heart? Or who will stand forth saying he is clean from sins? For we take the difference of these thus: the heart concerning the mind, and the sins concerning the deeds. Who will boast of having a pure heart, not defiled by falsely named knowledge, not defiled by a lie? Or who will stand forth saying he is clean from sins, having sinned nothing in the practical life?

If then we want to be saved, let us not, while occupied with the faith, neglect the life in practice, nor again put our trust in the life. From both let us know, grasp, believe that we shall have either the blameless or even the blessed — or the opposite of these.

Of the things for which people are punished, it is not only the frightful and terrible — which ought not even to be named among both — but also the things supposed to be lesser. For this reason the apostle seems to have listed, with the (if we must call them that) unlawful and abominable and defiling things, the things despised by the many.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: who will boast of a pure heart / clean from sins (LXX).
Quoted: falsely named knowledge.
Things that ought not even to be named.

translator_notes: Ἐγὼ νομίζω kept as 'I think'.
δοκεῖ kept as 'seems' in the apostle-listing sentence.
φρόνημα as 'mind' (the believing/knowing side), not later 'phronesis' jargon.
1 Corinthians 6 list opened at the section end; the named members follow on the next page.

title: Drunkard and reviler; is the soul blood?
english: Origen went on: With the (if we must call them that) unlawful and abominable and defiling things, the apostle seems also to have listed the things despised by the many. For what does he say? Do not be deceived: neither fornicators, nor adulterers, nor the soft, nor men who lie with men, nor thieves, nor drunkards, nor revilers will inherit the kingdom of God. You see: with evils of such size — the man who lies with men, the soft, the adulterer, the fornicator — he numbered the drunkard, the reviler, sins despised by all of us, so that we may be taught that we are not cast out of the kingdom of God for those only, but also for these that are thought to be smaller. Therefore let us neither revile, nor get drunk, nor seize, nor steal, nor do the things that are not lawful, even if we are led astray.
If anything is lacking concerning the rule, remind me. For the rest, we will speak to the scripture.
Dionysius said: Is the soul the blood?

Origen said: It has come to my hearing, and I say it as fully persuaded, that some of those here and of those in the neighboring towns think that after the departure from here the soul perceives nothing, but is in the tomb, in the body. And I know that I was carried more harshly on this matter against the other Heraclides and Celer who was before him — so harshly that he left and wanted to go away. And yet, for the sake of honor and of the word, he had sent for us. We came down into the discussion; he gave a statement, as that man cleared himself toward us with statements of faith [lacuna] that it was as toward God.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted vice-list (dump omits idolaters/greedy; wording of what is present is followed).

translator_notes: μαλακοί rendered 'the soft'; ἀρσενοκοῖται 'men who lie with men' — the Greek categories, not later English labels.
The locked quotation omits some members of the usual 1 Cor 6:9-10 list; the omission is not filled.
τὸν ἄλλον Ἡρακλείδαν: 'the other Heraclides', a different man from the bishop in the room.
Celer/Heraclides anecdote completed across the page cut; † ὅτι ὡς πρὸς Θεόν still left as [lacuna] in the next section's wording as well.

title: The texts that pull them aside; two men
english: Origen went on: We came down into the discussion; he gave a statement, as that man cleared himself toward us with statements of faith [lacuna] that it was as toward God.

Necessarily, then, beloved Dionysius inquires about this too. The texts by which they are pulled aside — lest any of them escape me — I will first set out, and to each, God granting, according to your prayer, we will answer.

What has pulled them aside is this: The soul of all flesh is blood. And this text has terribly stirred those who have not understood it. And You shall not eat the soul with the flesh; take strong care not to eat blood; you shall not eat the soul with the flesh. This is what has pulled them aside; for the other things that have pulled them aside are far less than the force of the sense in these.

I, for my part, praying to be helped in reading the divine things — for we need help so that we may not think something besides the truth — [lacuna]. I found that things not bodily are named with the same names as all the bodily things, so that the bodily things belong to the outer man, and the things with the same names as the bodily belong to the inner. Scripture says that the human being is two men: For if our outer man is being destroyed, yet our inner is being renewed day by day; and I delight in the law of God according to the inner man. These two men the apostle everywhere sets out, in each person.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: the soul of all flesh is blood (with Lev 17:14).
Soul/blood of flesh.
Quoted: you shall not eat the soul with the flesh; blood is the soul.
Blood/soul not to be eaten.
Quoted: outer man destroyed, inner renewed.
Quoted: I delight in the law according to the inner man.

translator_notes: † ὅτι ὡς πρὸς Θεόν left as [lacuna] in the Celer/Heraclides anecdote.
Ellipsis after φρονήσωμεν is a real gap in the dump; not filled.
ὁμωνύμως rendered 'with the same names' in the reading text; the technical homonymy is noted here.
περισπῶνται kept as 'pulled aside' (dragged off the sense).
Two-men sentence completed from the next page.

title: Not a human-shaped God; pearls and dogs
english: Origen went on: These two men the apostle everywhere sets out, in each person. And it seems to me he has not dared to innovate this account himself, but, having understood more nakedly what the scriptures said more obscurely, has spoken it.

Some think that in the Making of the World, after the creation of the human being, And God took dust from the earth and formed the human being is a repetition. It follows for these people that the 'according to the image' is the body, and that they grant God to be human-shaped, or that the form of God is according to this figure. But we are not so mad as to say either that God is composite from worse and better, so that the 'according to the image' would be on both, or that the whole [lacuna], God being, the 'according to the image' has come to be in the worse rather than in the better.

The words are rather fine; we need hearers who have a lean mind. I ask the hearers, then, to watch themselves, lest they ever become the cause of my being charged with throwing the holy things to dogs, to shameless souls. For the barking ones, the dog-like, those stretched toward fornications, toward revilings, do nothing else but yelp, and I must not throw the holy things to such as these. So too I ask the hearers not to become the cause of my being charged with setting pearls of such size — which we try to gather as good merchants — before those who wallow in the uncleannesses of bodies, and who for this reason are called swine.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: God took dust and formed the human being.
According to the image, misread as the body.
Holy things to dogs; pearls (continues next page).

translator_notes: δοκεῖ δέ μοι kept as 'it seems to me'.
† ὄντος τοῦ Θεοῦ in the image-argument left as [lacuna].
ἰσχνὴν διάνοιαν: 'lean mind' (thin, subtle), not 'sophisticated'.
βαϋβίζουσιν kept as 'yelp' (the onomatopoeia).
Pearls-before-swine sentence completed from the next page.

title: Swine, pearls, be transformed
english: Origen went on: I ask the hearers not to become the cause of my being charged with setting pearls of such size — which we try to gather as good merchants — before those who wallow in the uncleannesses of bodies, and who for this reason are called swine. For I would say that the one who is always rolling in bodily things and wallowing in the mire of life, and not hastening toward the clean life, toward the holy, is in all a swine.

If then, the kingdom of the heavens being likened to a man, a merchant seeking beautiful pearls, I find the beautiful pearls, and having bought them with toils and watchings I throw them to pleasure-loving souls, and to those wallowing in the mires around the bodily things and in the uncleannesses, I too shall have broken the law, because I threw the pearls to the swine. And the swine, receiving the pearls, since they do not see their beauty nor perceive their superiority, trample them — by speaking badly the things said well — and not only do they trample the pearls, but turning they also tear the servants of the pearls.

I beg you, then: be transformed. Do you want to learn that it is in you to be transformed, and to put off the form of the swine, which is according to the unclean soul, and the form of the dog, which is according to the barking and yelping and evil-speaking human being? And it is possible to be transformed from serpents. For an evil human being is called a serpent and offspring of vipers.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: kingdom likened to a merchant seeking pearls.
Pearls to swine; they trample and tear.
Be transformed (full quotation in section 14).
Be transformed — the imperative μεταμορφώθητε.

translator_notes: ἐφ' ἡμῖν in the next page is 'in our power'; here ἐν ὑμῖν ἔστιν τὸ μεταμορφωθῆναι is 'it is in you to be transformed'.
διακόνους τῶν μαργαριτῶν: 'servants of the pearls' (the teachers), torn when hearers turn.
Serpent clause completed from the next page.

title: From dogs, swine, serpents; fruits of repentance
english: Origen went on: And it is possible to be transformed from serpents. For an evil human being is called a serpent and offspring of vipers. If then we want to hear that it is in us to be transformed from serpents, from swine, from dogs, let us learn from the apostle the transformation that is in our power. For he says thus: And we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image.

If you were a barker and the Word formed you and remade you, you have been transformed from a dog into a human being. If you were unclean and the Word reached your soul and you offered yourself to the Word's forming, you have changed from a swine into a human being. If you were beast-like, hearing a word that tames, that domesticates, that changes you into a human being at the will of the Word, you will no longer hear serpent, offspring of vipers. For if it were impossible for these serpents — the serpents according to the soul through vice — to change, the Savior would not have said (or John): Make fruits worthy of repentance, then. Having repented you are no longer a serpent, offspring of vipers.

Since, then, it lies before us to speak about the human being, and to inquire about the soul of the human being whether it is not blood, and the word has required us to arrive at the account of two men in each person, and we have come to a mystical word, we ask you that I may not be charged because of you with throwing the pearls to swine, the holy things to dogs, with casting the divine things to the serpents, with giving a share of the tree of life to the serpent.

added_allusions.reason: Serpent / offspring of vipers (with 12:34; 23:33).
Offspring of vipers.
Quoted: unveiled face, transformed into the same image.
Quoted: make fruits worthy of repentance (Matthew 3:8).
Same fruits-of-repentance saying.
Pearls / holy things refrain.

translator_notes: ἐφ' ἡμῖν μεταμόρφωσιν: 'the transformation that is in our power' — Origen's hedge that change is possible, not automatic.
ἢ ὁ Ἰωάννης kept: 'the Savior (or John)' — Origen will not force the speaker of the fruits saying.
λόγος as 'Word' when it forms/tames; 'word' when it is the discussion.
Pearls/dogs/serpents charge completed from the next page.

title: Agony of speaking; inside and outside; the first man
english: Origen went on: We ask you that I may not be charged because of you with throwing the pearls to swine, the holy things to dogs, with casting the divine things to the serpents, with giving a share of the tree of life to the serpent. That I may not be charged, be transformed: put away malice, faction, anger, fights, wrath, griefs, discord, so that there may no longer be schisms among you, but that you may be fitted together in the same mind and the same judgment.

I am in agony both to speak and not to speak. Because of those who are worthy I want to speak, lest I be charged with having deprived of the word those able to hear. Because of those who are not worthy I hesitate to speak, because of what has been said already, lest I ever throw the holy things to dogs and cast the pearls to the swine.

It was the work of Jesus alone to know how to separate, among the hearers, those outside from those inside, so that to those outside he may speak in parables, and to those who have entered his house he may loose the parables. The 'outside' and the entering into the house is mystical. For what is it to me to judge those outside? Everyone who sins is outside. For this reason let it be spoken in parables to those outside, if somehow they may be able, leaving the outside, to become inside. Entering the house is mystical: the genuine disciple of Jesus enters Jesus' house; he enters by thinking the things of the church, by living in the church's way. The inside and the outside is spiritual.

You see how much I say in a preface, preparing the hearers. I hesitate to speak, being about to put it off even while speaking. What do I want to do? To take a word that heals the souls of those who hear.

The human being, then, being created, was first created the one according to the image, of whom matter is not found. For the one according to the image is not from matter either. And God said: Let us make a human being according to our image and according to our likeness, and let them rule, and the rest.

added_allusions.reason: Tree of life given to the serpent — the charge Origen fears.
Tree of life, lest the serpent-hearer take it.
Put away malice, wrath, anger.
Same put-away list.
Quoted: no schisms; same mind and judgment.
Parables to those outside; loosed inside the house.
To those outside everything in parables.
Quoted: what is it to me to judge those outside?
Quoted: let us make according to our image (continues next page).

translator_notes: Ἀγωνιῶ καὶ εἰπεῖν, ἀγωνιῶ καὶ μὴ εἰπεῖν kept as doubled agony.
ἐάν πως kept as 'if somehow'.
First creation κατ' εἰκόνα is immaterial — Origen's two-stage anthropology, not a later 'double creation' slogan in the reading text.
Genesis 1:26 completed across the page cut.

title: Image without dust; eyes of the inner man
english: Origen went on: And God said, Let us make a human being according to our image and according to our likeness, and let them rule, and the rest. And God made the human being — not taking dust from the earth as in the case of the second, but according to the image of God he made him.

And that the 'according to the image of God' is known as immaterial, better than every bodily subsistence, not by Moses only but also by the apostle, his wording shows when he says: Having put off the old man with his deeds and having put on the new, the one being renewed unto knowledge according to the image of the one who created him.

There are, then, two men in each of us. How is it said, The soul of all flesh is blood? The problem is great. As, then, the outer man is named with the same name as the inner, so also his members, so that one may say that every member of the outer man is also named according to the inner man.

The outer man has eyes, and the inner is said to have eyes: Lighten my eyes, lest I sleep unto death. He is not speaking about these eyes, nor about perceptible sleep, nor about the common death. The commandment of the Lord is bright, lighting the eyes. It is not that by keeping the Lord's commandments we become sharper-sighted according to the body, but that by keeping the divine commandments we become sharper-sighted according to the mind. The eyes of the inner man see through more than ours: Uncover my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of your law.

added_allusions.reason: Let them rule; according to the image he made him.
The second forming from dust, distinguished from the image.
Quoted: put off the old, put on the new according to the image of the one who created.
The problem verse: soul of all flesh is blood.
Quoted: lighten my eyes, lest I sleep unto death (LXX 12:4).
Quoted: the commandment of the Lord is bright, lighting the eyes (LXX 18:9).
Quoted: uncover my eyes (LXX 118:18; continues next page).

translator_notes: Scherer [16] splits ἡμετέραν; completed at the page start.
Two men 'in each of us' — Origen's payoff, not a second human species.
μέγα τὸ πρόβλημα kept: 'the problem is great'.
Psalm 119:18 completed so the section does not hang mid-quote.

title: Eyes of the mind; ears in our power
english: Origen went on: Uncover my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of your law — not as though his eyes were covered, but our eyes are the mind. It belongs to Jesus alone to uncover, so that we may be able to behold the things written and to understand the things said in a hidden way.

The outer man has ears, and the inner man is said to have ears. He who has ears to hear, let him hear. All had the ears of sense, but not all had succeeded in having the inner hearings cleansed. These ears are not in our power; those are in our power. And since it is in our power to have those ears, for this reason the prophet says: Hear, you deaf, and you blind, look up to see. And who is deaf but my servants, and who is blind but those who lord it over them? And the slaves of God were blinded.

That it is in our power to become deaf [lacuna] (let us attend; what is said is about to touch all of us; the inner man must be described so that the blood may be found) — that it is in our power to become deaf according to those hearings, hear the prophet saying: The sinners have been alienated from the womb; they have gone astray from the belly; they have spoken falsehoods. Wrath is theirs according to the likeness of the serpent, as of a deaf asp that stops her ears, which will not listen to the voice of charmers, of a drug being mixed by a wise man.

added_allusions.reason: End of uncover-my-eyes quotation.
Quoted: he who has ears to hear, let him hear.
Quoted: hear, you deaf; who is blind but my servants.
Quoted: alienated from the womb; wrath as a serpent (LXX 57:4-5; continues next page).

translator_notes: Ellipsis after κωφωθῆναι is a gap; the parenthetical 'let us attend' is in the dump and is kept.
ταῦτα τὰ ὦτα οὐκ ἐφ' ἡμῖν, ἐκεῖνα ἐφ' ἡμῖν: outer ears not in our power, inner ears are — a load-bearing distinction.
ὡς κεκαλυμμένων αὐτοῦ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν οὐχί kept: 'not as though his eyes were covered'.
Deaf-asp psalm completed across the page cut.

title: The deaf asp; fragrance of Christ
english: Origen went on from the psalm: Wrath is theirs according to the likeness of the serpent, as of a deaf asp that stops her ears, which will not listen to the voice of charmers, of a drug being mixed by a wise man.

And you, as many as know yourselves to be at fault, if you hear a word and a drug being mixed by a wise man, and you hear words of charmers, so that it may settle your wrath and your vice, and then you stop your ears, not opening them nor spreading them for the reception of what is said — the word will reach you: Wrath is theirs according to the likeness of the serpent, as of a deaf asp that stops her ears, which will not listen to the voice of charmers, of a drug being mixed by a wise man.

The outer man smells with nostrils, receiving fragrance and stench. And the inner man receives the fragrance of righteousness and the stench of sins with other nostrils — fragrance, as the apostle teaches, saying: We are the fragrance of Christ to God in every place, among those being saved and among those perishing: to the one a smell from death to death, to the other a smell from life to life. And Solomon too says in the Song of Songs, in the person of the young women, the daughters of Jerusalem: After you we will run to the smell of your ointments. As, then, with the nostrils we receive perceptible fragrance and perceptible stench, so according to the inner man there is a reception, in the one who is healthy according to the divine senses, of the fragrance of righteousness.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: deaf asp, charmers, drug of a wise man (LXX 57:5-6).
Quoted: fragrance of Christ; smell from death / from life.
Quoted: we will run to the smell of your ointments (LXX 1:3-4).

translator_notes: φάρμακον kept as 'drug' (charm-mixture), not modern 'medicine' or 'poison' only.
Origen applies the asp psalm to hearers who stop their ears against the present word — the turn is kept.
Nostril analogy completed from the next page.

title: Stench, taste, and the woman's touch
english: Origen went on: As with the nostrils we receive perceptible fragrance and perceptible stench, so according to the inner man there is a reception, in the one who is healthy according to the divine senses, of the fragrance of righteousness, which the apostle had, and of the stench of sins. What stench of sins? About which the prophet says thus: My bruises have grown rancid and rotten from the face of my folly.
The outer man has the tasting faculty, and the inner man has the spiritual tasting faculty, about which it is said: Taste and see that the Lord is kind.

The outer man has perceptible touch, and the inner man has touch — that touch by which the woman with the flow of blood touched the hem of Jesus. She touched. For the one who said, Who touched me? bore witness. And a little before, Peter was saying to him: The crowds are pressing you, and you say, Who touched me? He thinks that those who touch bodily are touching, not spiritually. So those pressing Jesus were not touching him; for they were not touching him by faith. But she alone, having a certain divine touch, touched Jesus and for this reason was healed. And since she touched with his divine touch, for this reason power of Jesus went out upon her divine touch.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: my bruises have grown rancid from my folly (LXX 37:6).
Quoted: taste and see that the Lord is kind (LXX 33:9).
Woman with the flow; who touched me; crowds pressing (Mark 5:25-31).
Power gone out; Peter/crowds.
Hem of the garment.

translator_notes: χρηστός kept as 'kind' (the tasting psalm), not 'Christ' wordplay unless the Greek makes it.
θεῖά τις ἁφή: 'a certain divine touch' — Origen's hedge τις kept.
Power-going-out clause completed from the next page.

title: Hands, feet, the wise man's head
english: Origen went on: And since she touched with his divine touch, for this reason power of Jesus went out upon her divine touch. He says then: Who touched me? For I knew power had gone out from me.

About this more divine touch John speaks: And our hands handled concerning the word of life. So we have other hands, about which it is said: The lifting of my hands is an evening sacrifice. For if I lift these hands, but the hands of my soul lie below, and I do not lift them through holy and good deeds, the lifting of my hands does not become an evening sacrifice.

I have other feet as well, about which Solomon promised me, saying: Your foot shall not stumble. Something [strange] is said in Ecclesiastes. To the one who does not understand it will seem senseless; but to the wise it has been said from Ecclesiastes: The eyes of the wise man are in his head. In what head? For of every human being, even of the senseless and the fool, the perceptible eyes are in a perceptible head; but the eyes of the wise man, the ones spoken of before, the ones lit by the Lord's commandment, are in his head — in Christ, since the head of a man is Christ, the apostle says. The thinking faculty is in Christ. My belly, my belly I ache, said Jeremiah.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: I knew power had gone out from me.
Quoted: our hands handled concerning the word of life.
Quoted: lifting of my hands an evening sacrifice (LXX 140:2).
Your foot shall not stumble.
Foot not dashed — possible parallel.
Quoted: the wise man's eyes are in his head.
Quoted: the head of a man is Christ.
Quoted: my belly, my belly I ache (continues next page).

translator_notes: κέωνται treated as κεῖνται 'lie'; flagged as a likely dump form.
<ἄτοπόν> is an editor supplement already in the locked text; rendered '[strange]' and noted.
The Ecclesiastes saying is called ἄτοπον / seeming ἀνόητον — Origen's wonder is kept.
Jeremiah's belly cry completed from the next page.

title: Belly, bones, and the saw
english: Origen went on: My belly, my belly I ache, said Jeremiah. What belly does he ache with? The one we too ache with — the belly with which, since he was in labor for the people, I ache in my belly, and the senses, not these but of my heart.

If I come even to the fine parts of the body, I see them without flesh upon the soul. Lord, do not rebuke me in your wrath, nor discipline me in your anger. Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak; heal me, Lord, for my bones were troubled. What bones of the prophet were troubled? The harmony of his soul and the firmness of his mind were troubled, and he asks for the restoration of those bones.

Our bones were scattered beside Hades. What bones of the speaker were scattered beside Hades? If you see for me the one who has sinned, and you see his harmonies in the region of sin, in the region of the dead, in the region of vice, you will say of such a one that his bones were scattered. All my bones will say: Lord, who is like you? These bones speak, converse, say, perceive God — and these [bodily bones] are without sensation, as physicians' pupils show when they saw bones of one who does not perceive in the sawing. All my bones, then, will say: Lord, who is like you? Bones the inner man has, all of them.

added_allusions.reason: Belly in labor; senses of my heart.
Quoted: do not rebuke in wrath; my bones were troubled (LXX 6:2-3).
Quoted: our bones were scattered beside Hades (LXX 140:7).
Quoted: all my bones will say, Lord, who is like you (LXX 34:10).

translator_notes: Jeremiah's belly clause is compressed in the dump; rendered close, not expanded into a smoother commentary.
ἄσαρκα ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχήν: 'without flesh upon the soul' — the inner members are not meat.
The sawing comparison is Origen's, kept.
Inner-man bones clause completed from the next page.

title: Lost heart, numbered hairs, inner blood
english: Origen went on: Bones the inner man has, all of them. The inner man has a heart: Hear me, you who have lost the heart. Those people had this heart of the body; for that heart is not lost. But when someone neglects the cultivation of the intelligent condition, and from much idleness puts away the thinking faculty, he has lost the heart, and it is said to such a one: Hear me, you who have lost the heart.

And the hairs of your head are all numbered. What hairs? For which reason they were Nazirites spiritually. Since you have all these things of the perceptible body in the case of the inner man, no longer hesitate also about the blood, that with the same name as the perceptible blood, as with the other members of the body, there is blood according to the inner man.

That blood of a sinful soul is poured out. For the blood of your souls shall be required. He did not say 'your blood,' but the blood of your souls. And The blood from the hand of the watchman I will require. What blood does God require from the hand of the watchman, if not that which is poured out of the sinner? So the heart of the fool is lost, and it is said, Hear me, you who have lost the heart, as the blood is poured out and the vital power of the soul.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: hear me, you who have lost the heart (LXX form).
Quoted: hairs of your head all numbered (Luke 12:7).
Nazirite hair — spiritual reading.
Quoted: the blood of your souls shall be required.
Quoted: blood from the hand of the watchman I will require.

translator_notes: Δι' ὃ ἦσαν πνευματικῶς ναζιραῖοι is terse; rendered 'For which reason they were Nazirites spiritually,' not expanded.
The blood argument is the delayed answer to Dionysius: inner blood, not the vein-blood of Lev 17.
οὐκ εἶπεν Τὸ αἷμα ὑμῶν kept: 'He did not say your blood.'
Vital-power clause completed from the next page — the delayed answer to 'is the soul the blood?'

title: Better to depart and be with Christ
english: Origen went on: So the heart of the fool is lost, and it is said, Hear me, you who have lost the heart, as the blood is poured out and the vital power of the soul.

If the soul has been understood, and understood according to the inner man, and it has been understood that in that one is the 'according to the image,' it is clear that Paul says well: For it is better to depart and to be with Christ. Before the resurrection the righteous man is with Christ, and in that very soul he lives with Christ. For this reason: For it is better to depart and to be with Christ.

But according to you who say that the soul lies in the tomb with the body, it has not gone out from the body, it does not rest, it has not come to be in the paradise of God, it does not rest in Abraham's bosom. And according to you who say such things, it is not better to depart and to be with Christ; for he is not with Christ at the moment of departing, if the soul is blood. If the soul lies in the tombs, how can it be with Christ?

But according to me and the word of God, the soul that has departed from the labors, that has departed from the sweats, that has been released from the body, that can say, Now you release your servant, Master, in peace, goes out in peace and rests with Christ. So Abraham's soul heard: And you shall go to your fathers in peace, nourished in a good old age. He goes away to the fathers. Which fathers? About whom Paul says: For this reason I bend my knees to the Father, from whom every family.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted twice: better to depart and be with Christ.
Paradise of God — the soul gone out, not in the tomb.
Abraham's bosom.
Quoted: now you release your servant in peace.
Quoted: you shall go to your fathers in peace.

translator_notes: πρὸ τῆς ἀναστάσεως σὺν Χριστῷ: the righteous with Christ before the resurrection — kept, against the tomb-sleepers.
κατὰ δὲ ὑμᾶς: 'according to you' — Origen turns on the blood=soul party in the room.
'Which fathers?' completed from the next page.

title: Ready for death; Demetrius on immortality
english: Origen went on: He goes away to the fathers. Which fathers? About whom Paul says: For this reason I bend my knees to the Father, from whom every family. Thus according to us Aaron was released. For it is also written in Ecclesiastes about the righteous man who has contested well, who has gone out from the bodily bond, that He shall come out of the house of prisoners to reign.

Thus I am persuaded to die for the truth; thus I despise the so-called death, ready; thus — bring beasts, bring crosses, bring fire, bring tortures. I know that at the moment of being released I go out of the body; I rest with Christ. For this reason let us contest, for this reason let us wrestle, let us groan being in the body — not as about to be in the tombs again at once, in the body, but as about to be released, and as changing the body toward the more spiritual. And being about to depart and be with Christ, how do we groan, we who are in the body?
When bishop Philip had entered, Demetrius, another bishop, said: Brother Origen teaches that the soul is immortal.

Origen said: Bishop Demetrius's word has given us the beginning of another problem. He said we had said that the soul is immortal. To this word I will say that the soul is both immortal and the soul is not immortal.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: I bend my knees to the Father, from whom every family.
Aaron was released / gathered — possible (dump: ἀπελύθη Ἀαρών).
Quoted: he shall come out of the house of prisoners to reign (LXX).
Groan being in the body.
Groan in the tent / body.
Depart and be with Christ, reprise.
Body changed toward the more spiritual.

translator_notes: ἀπελύθη Ἀαρών: 'Aaron was released' as printed; not expanded to a full Numbers narrative.
ἐξελεύσε [τα]ι restored as ἐξελεύσεται (obvious wrap in a quotation).
φέρε θηρία... kept as live imperatives: 'bring beasts...'.
Philip's entrance is narrative in the minutes, not a speech.
πάπα Δημητρίου rendered 'Bishop Demetrius' (same Greek πάπα as Heraclides; not later 'Pope').
Immortality sentence completed into the next page's opening.

title: Three deaths; immortal and not immortal
english: Origen said: To this word I will say that the soul is both immortal and the soul is not immortal. Let us first distinguish the name of death and how many things are signified from the utterance 'death.' I will try to set out how many things are signified, not according to the Greeks, but how many are signified according to the divine scripture. Perhaps someone wiser than I will also set out other significations; I, at any rate, for the present know three deaths. What are these three deaths?
Someone lives to God and has died to sin, according to the apostle. This death is blessed: someone dies to sin. This death my Lord died. For that which he died, he died to sin.
I know another death as well, according to which someone dies to God, about which it is said: The soul that sins, it shall die.
I know also a third death, according to which we commonly think those released from the body have died. For Adam lived thirty and nine hundred years, and he died.

There being, then, three deaths, let us see whether the human soul is immortal according to the three deaths, or not according to the three deaths, but immortal according to some of them. According to the middle death we all die, which we take to be dissolution. This death no human soul dies. For if it died, it would not be punished after death.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: died to sin; live to God (with 6:2).
Died to sin.
Quoted: the soul that sins, it shall die (18:20).
Same soul-that-sins saying.
Quoted: Adam lived 930 years and died (dump: thirty and nine hundred).

translator_notes: ἴσως μέν μου σοφώτερος kept: 'Perhaps someone wiser than I'.
Three deaths listed as (1) death to sin, (2) death to God, (3) common bodily death. 'Middle death' then = dissolution; the numbering is Origen's, not regularized.
οὐ καθ' Ἕλληνας: not according to the Greeks — kept.
No-soul-dies clause completed from the next page.

title: They will seek death; Balaam; perhaps not always mortal
english: Origen went on: This death no human soul dies. For if it died, it would not be punished after death. Human beings, he says, will seek death and will not find it. For the souls being punished will seek death; they will want rather not to be than to be and be punished. For this reason human beings will seek death and will not find it. According to this signification every human soul is immortal.

But according to the remaining significations, according to the one the soul is mortal, and blessed if it dies to sin. About this death Balaam, prophesying, spoke, praying in a divine spirit: May my soul die in the souls of the righteous. About this death Balaam prophesied in a strange way, and he prayed the finest things for himself in the word of God. For he prayed to die to sin in order to live to God. And for this reason he said: May my soul die in the souls of the righteous, and may my seed be as the seed of these.

And there is another death, according to which we are not immortal, but we are able, from keeping watch, not to die. And perhaps the mortal of the soul is not always mortal. For so long as it admits of sinning such a sin that it becomes the soul that sins, it shall die, the soul is mortal of the real death. But if it comes to be in firmness of blessedness so as to be incapable of death, the one that has the eternal life is no longer mortal, but has become immortal according to this signification too.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: they will seek death and not find it.
Quoted: may my soul die in the souls of the righteous.
Die to sin, live to God — Balaam read this way.
The soul that sins shall die, reprise.

translator_notes: Scherer [26] is not a missing page: DCO prints ἀπο26 θνῄσκει for ἀπο[26]θνῄσκει. Disclosed, not invented.
τάχα kept: 'And perhaps the mortal of the soul is not always mortal.'
δυνά-μεθα hyphen joined as δυνάμεθα.
παραδόξως: 'in a strange way' — Balaam's prayer is odd until read as death-to-sin.
Blessedness clause completed from the next page.

title: He who alone has immortality; life set before us
english: Origen went on: But if the soul comes to be in firmness of blessedness so as to be incapable of death, the one that has the eternal life is no longer mortal, but has become immortal according to this signification too.
How has it been said by the apostle, He who alone has immortality, of God? I am searching in order to find that Christ Jesus died for all apart from God. You have how God alone has immortality.

Let us take up the eternal life, then; let us take it up from what is in our power. God does not give it to us, but sets it before us: See, I have given life before your face. It is in our power to stretch out the hand, to act with good deeds, and to take the life and store it in the soul.

This life is Christ, who said, I am the life. This life which now is present to the righteous in a shadow, but then face to face. For the spirit before our face is Christ the Lord, of whom we said: In his shadow we shall live among the nations. If your shadow of the life grants such goods — such as Moses had when prophesying, such as Isaiah had when seeing the Lord Sabaoth sitting on a throne high and lifted up, such as Jeremiah had when hearing, Before I formed you in the belly I know you, and before I formed you in the belly I know you, and before you came out of the womb I consecrated you — such as Ezekiel had when seeing the cherubim, seeing the wheels, the unspeakable mysteries — how shall we live when we no longer live under the shadow of the life, but come to be in the life itself?

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: he who alone has immortality.
Quoted in Origen's form: died for all apart from God (χωρὶς Θεοῦ, not χάριτι Θεοῦ).
Quoted: see, I have given life before your face (30:19).
Life and death set before you.
Quoted: I am the life (11:25).
I am the resurrection and the life.
Quoted: then face to face.
Quoted: the spirit before our face is Christ the Lord; in his shadow we shall live (LXX).
Quoted: the Lord Sabaoth sitting on a throne high and lifted up.
Quoted, with the first clause doubled in the dump.

translator_notes: χωρὶς Θεοῦ kept: 'apart from God' — Origen's Hebrews reading, the reason only the Father 'alone has immortality'. Not replaced with 'by the grace of God'.
Οὐ δίδωσιν αὐτὴν ἡμῖν ὁ Θεός, ἀλλὰ παρατίθησιν kept: God does not give the life, but sets it before us.
ἐκ τοῦ ἐφ' ἡμῖν: 'from what is in our power'.
Jeremiah 1:5 first clause is doubled in the locked dump; both copies kept, not silently trimmed.
Ζητῶ ἵν' εὕρω kept: 'I am searching in order to find'.
Jeremiah-to-Ezekiel list completed from the last page so the shadow-into-life question can be read here.

title: From the shadow into the life
english: Origen went on from Jeremiah's call: Before I formed you in the belly I know you, and before you came out of the womb I consecrated you — such as Ezekiel had when seeing the cherubim, seeing the wheels, the unspeakable mysteries — how shall we live when we no longer live under the shadow of the life, but come to be in the life itself?

For now our life is hidden with Christ; but when Christ, our life, is manifested, then we too will be manifested with him in glory. Let us hasten toward this life, groaning, grieving that we are in the tent, that we are at home in the body. So long as we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord. Let us long to be away from the body and at home with the Lord, so that being at home with him we may become one toward the God of all, and [perhaps: behold] his only-begotten Son, being saved in all things and becoming blessed, in Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the power unto the ages of the ages.

translator_notes: Editor restorations in the last sentence: [Κύριον] is the Pauline word and is read; [καὶ] left light; [ὁρῶμεν] is not treated as certain Origen — marked 'perhaps: behold'.
No Amen is added; the dump ends at τῶν αἰώνων.
σκιὰ τῆς ζωῆς: 'shadow of the life' — even Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel lived under the shadow; the face is still to come.
